correctness.rationale: Metric distance and adjacency are automorphism invariants, so distinct listed classes cannot merge. Conversely, two ordered off-diagonal pairs with the same distance and adjacency bit induce isomorphic two-point metric-graph substructures; strict homogeneity extends that two-point isomorphism to a global automorphism. The finite-extension property realizes both adjacency choices at every canonical distance level. Singleton homogeneity gives one diagonal orbit. These steps prove exhaustiveness and nonemptiness directly from the primary construction.

final_claim: For the Kubiś--Pech--Pech universal homogeneous ultrametric graph on Baire space, ordered pairs have exactly one diagonal orbit and, at each positive distance \(2^{-k}\), exactly two off-diagonal automorphism orbits distinguished by adjacency; equivalently every point stabilizer has exactly two nontrivial orbits on each metric sphere.
